name: MA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Stephen Lynch running with a large cash advantage
Republican Robert Burke has raised essentially nothing and has negative cash on hand
Prediction markets price Lynch near 97% to win
model.rationale: Lynch is a well-funded incumbent in a Boston-area district that leans 15 points Democratic, while Burke has no fundraising footprint and carries debt. Markets price Lynch around 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A surprise outside-spending surge against Lynch or an unusually strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though not realistically the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' 8th District is a solidly Democratic Boston-area seat with a 15-point Democratic partisan lean. Stephen Lynch, the longtime incumbent, is running for reelection and holds a decisive financial edge, with roughly $640,000 on hand after raising over $900,000. Some outside spending has been directed against him, but nothing suggests a competitive race.

Republican Robert Burke has raised no money and reports negative cash on hand, leaving him without the resources to contest a district this favorable to Democrats. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but lacks any visible campaign infrastructure. Prediction markets price Lynch's chances near 97%, and with no public polling or expert ratings to suggest otherwise, the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
